HOOK_TITLE:
Preparing students for real life,
not outdated tests
HERO_H1: HTA is the only school in Kazakhstan that develops the skills students need in the age of AI
HERO_SUB: In a world where AI generates answers in seconds, children need skills that cannot be automated: critical thinking, courage, empathy, and the ability to turn ideas into reality
HERO_BOX_1: An international school fully accredited by CIS and WASC
HERO_BOX_2: A Korda-Method School develops essential 21st-century skills
HERO_BOX_3: The Minerva Baccalaureate is an innovative, academically advanced program for grades 10–12
WHY_QUOTE: If we teach today’s students as we taught yesterday’s, we rob them of tomorrow
WHY_H1: The world has changed. Schools must change with it
WHY_TEXT_1: For decades, success in school meant memorizing information, following instructions, and giving expected answers. That approach is outdated.
WHY_TEXT_2:
Today, AI creates texts, code, and solutions faster than any expert.
The key question for parents is not what a child will know, but what they will be able to do with that knowledge.
WHY_BOX: Will my child know what to do when the answer is unclear, the problem is real, and the solution could change people’s lives? This is exactly what students learn at HTA.
CARD_1_TEXT: AI is already handling routine tasks. What remains for us are the things algorithms cannot do: think critically, negotiate, collaborate, and find solutions where there are no ready-made answers.
CARD_2_TITLE: The world needs creators, not consumers
CARD_2_TEXT: Employers no longer need people who simply follow instructions. They are looking for those who can ask the right questions and create something new.
CARD_3_TEXT: In 10 years, there will be professions that do not even exist today. Schools must prepare students for life in a world transformed by AI.
WHY_HTA_H1: HTA is the only school in Kazakhstan that has built a learning system designed for professional and personal success in a world inevitably transformed by AI.
WHY_HTA_TEXT: Learning at HTA is not about accumulating knowledge, but about applying it in real life.
KORDA_H1: Skills are developed through practice and action
KORDA_TEXT_1: The Korda Method is an approach to learning that shifts the focus from WHAT students learn to HOW they learn.
KORDA_TEXT_2: Project-based learning immerses students in real-life challenges. They learn to identify problems, deeply explore context and user needs, test ideas, and present their solutions to industry experts.
KORDA_TEXT_3: Feedback is not about grades — it is about questions and coaching from experts who help students recognize the strengths and weaknesses of their solutions and deepen their understanding of the problem. Students refine their projects, try again, and learn not to fear mistakes. This is how they develop flexible thinking, inner resilience, and the confidence to act in uncertain situations.
PROJECT_1_TASK: Project challenge: develop solutions to reduce violence against children
PROJECT_2_TASK: Project challenge: develop solutions to reduce incidents in the mountains
PROJECT_3_TITLE: A New Sports Complex for HTA
PROJECT_3_TASK: Project challenge: Develop a concept for a new sports complex that will replace the existing one.
ENTRE_H1: The mindset people need when the future cannot be predicted
ENTRE_TEXT_1: Over the course of a year, students move from solving real challenges faced by Kazakhstani businesses to building their own startups. They develop entrepreneurial skills and learn to navigate uncertainty while solving meaningful real-world problems.
ENTRE_TEXT_2: We do not aim to raise entrepreneurs. We develop an entrepreneurial mindset: the ability to identify problems, test ideas, make decisions, and create value for society.
MBACC_H1: An academically advanced program for high school students
MBACC_TEXT:
Learning is based on the Flipped-Classroom model, where students independently study new material before class, while classroom time is dedicated to discussions, practice, problem-solving, and teamwork. This format helps develop critical thinking, independence, communication skills, and the ability to apply knowledge in practice.
The learning outcome directly depends on the quality of students’ independent preparation and their active participation during lessons. Instruction is delivered in English.
Graduates receive two diplomas — a Kazakhstani state-recognized diploma and the Minerva Baccalaureate (USA)
CHILDHOOD_QUOTE: It is impossible to predict who a child will become. We can only create the conditions in which they begin to grow and flourish.
LIFE_QUOTE: Education is not preparation for life; education is life itself
VOICES_STAT: 92% of HTA students say they love their school
FINAL_QUOTE_1: In the 21st century, we may witness the rise of a massive “useless class”… This class will not only be unemployed — it will be unemployable.
FINAL_QUOTE_2: Curiosity, courage, creativity, compassion, and communication are becoming especially important skills in the age of AI.

GRADUATE_COMMUNITY_TITLE: Become part of the HTA community.
GRADUATE_DREAMER_TEXT: HTA graduates think boldly and freely about innovative ideas and find inspiration in the process of exploring new ones.
GRADUATE_CRITICAL_THINKER_TEXT: HTA graduates think beyond society’s imposed boundaries, consider different perspectives, and draw conclusions based on analysis and objective evaluation.
GRADUATE_LIFELONG_LEARNER_TEXT: HTA graduates are curious and growth-oriented. They find joy in the process of discovering and learning new things.
GRADUATE_COLLABORATIVE_TEXT: HTA graduates understand that the art of collaboration in pursuit of a shared goal requires the willingness to contribute thoughtfully and respectfully, stay open to differing perspectives, and value the ideas of others.
GRADUATE_GLOBAL_CITIZEN_TEXT: HTA graduates actively contribute to their communities and understand that all people are united by a shared humanity that transcends geographic, political, and cultural boundaries.
GRADUATE_PROBLEM_SOLVER_TEXT: HTA graduates embrace complex challenges with courage and resilience. They analyze problems deeply and thoughtfully to develop creative, data-informed solutions.
GRADUATE_SKILLED_COMMUNICATOR_TEXT: HTA graduates are proficient in multiple languages and demonstrate a deep understanding of their audience and context, enabling them to engage in meaningful dialogue.
GRADUATE_EMOTIONAL_TEXT: HTA graduates possess a high level of emotional intelligence. They understand the emotions of others, recognize the nuances of interpersonal relationships, navigate complex situations effectively, and demonstrate an understanding of other people’s motivations and goals
COMMUNITY_MESSAGE_TITLE: A school where teachers believe in you.
MBACC_COMPARISON_TITLE: Most programs prepare students for exams. MBacc prepares them for life
MBACC_COMPARISON_SUBTITLE: Comparison of leading high school programs
MBACC_COMPARISON_IB_POINT_1: Six subjects over two years, with an intensive examination period at the end. The results determine the final diploma score.
MBACC_COMPARISON_IB_POINT_2: Final exams make up a large portion of the grade — two years of work are assessed during a single examination session.
MBACC_COMPARISON_CAMBRIDGE_POINT_1: Students study 3–4 subjects in depth and spend two years preparing for written examinations, which are the main and often the only assessment criterion.
MBACC_COMPARISON_CAMBRIDGE_POINT_2: Almost the entire grade depends on final written examinations — coursework in most subjects is minimal or absent.
MBACC_COMPARISON_AP_POINT_1: College-level courses for high school students are built around a standardized exam in each subject once per year. Only the exam result counts for college credit.
MBACC_COMPARISON_AP_POINT_2: One exam, one day, one grade — the value of the entire course is determined by the result of a single test.
MBACC_COMPARISON_MBACC_POINT_1: A hybrid program focused on skills development. Students learn to think, collaborate, and solve problems in any subject. There are no final exams. Progress is tracked continuously.
MBACC_COMPARISON_MBACC_POINT_2: Continuous feedback instead of exams. Progress is assessed throughout the entire learning journey, not on a single day
VOICES_QUOTE_1: "I love HTA because I enjoy being here. The teachers are kind, and I can learn English."
VOICES_QUOTE_2: “Because it’s very good and there are good people and I feel safe”.
VOICES_QUOTE_3:
"I love HTA because of the environment it creates. Here, you don't just memorize information — you learn how to think, analyze, and apply knowledge in real-life situations. The project-based approach helps students take responsibility and work effectively as a team.
What I especially value is that there are people who support and motivate you. Teachers don't just explain topics; they are genuinely invested in your growth.
For me, HTA is a place where I am not just studying, but developing as a person. I am learning to make decisions, make mistakes, draw conclusions, and keep moving forward."
VOICES_QUOTE_4: "I love HTA because we have rock climbing, physical education, and math classes."
VOICES_QUOTE_6: "Because the school has a good learning program and provides food options for people who cannot have milk. There is a long lunch break, kind teachers, desserts on Wednesdays, and good, balanced meals."
VOICES_QUOTE_7:
"I love HTA because it allows me to discover and develop who I am. At the same time, I don't feel the pressure of a traditional 5-point grading system. This helps me set my own priorities and develop my skills gradually, at my own pace.
There are many more reasons why I love my school, but there are so many that I couldn't possibly list them all here."
VOICES_QUOTE_8: "I feel safe here. And I know that every idea I have will be supported by a teacher, who will help me develop it further."
VOICES_RESEARCH_QUOTE_1:

ENTRE_2025_UVU_TASK: Project challenge: create a plan for UvU to launch 1,000 eco-shuttles across the city within 3 years and capture the Almaty market
ENTRE_2025_ALMATY_AIR_TASK: Project challenge: develop a plan for a new organization that will significantly improve air quality in Almaty
ENTRE_2025_AMIRAN_TASK: Project challenge: develop a strategy for Amiran to become profitable within 9 months while staying true to the company’s mission. The strategy should work within the company’s current capabilities
ENTRE_2025_BARYTAN_TEXT: Initiative: students developed a technology that automatically transforms a doctor-patient conversation into a structured medical record, saving time and simplifying the process of documenting data
ENTRE_2025_RAYHEART_TEXT: Initiative: students developed a smart medical corset with built-in biosensors that continuously monitor heart performance, helping prevent and provide early warning of a repeated heart attack
ENTRE_2025_NEXTSTEP_TEXT: Initiative: students developed a two-week interactive summer camp for teenagers aged 15–18 that helps them prepare for independent life in a safe environment by developing practical skills related to real finances and everyday tasks
ENTRE_2024_PLATFORMA_TASK: Project challenge: develop a plan to capture the Almaty and Kazakhstan markets for Platforma Market
ENTRE_2024_KAZBEEF_TASK: Project challenge: develop a plan to create a new organization that will solve desertification in Kazakhstan. Justify the proposal through a comprehensive analysis of existing and potential solutions to this problem
ENTRE_2024_SHINLINE_TASK: Project challenge: create a strategy for the Shin-Line product to become a market leader across the post-Soviet region
ENTRE_2024_SILVER_PEAR_TEXT: Initiative: students addressed food waste by turning it into compost and animal feed, reducing environmental harm and supporting sustainable agriculture. The product was successfully tested at Dostyk Residence
ENTRE_2024_TAN_TEXT: Initiative: students created a coffee drink brand with a “be your own barista” concept, allowing users to create their own drinks through a unique three-tier design
ENTRE_2024_PETX_TEXT: Initiative: students addressed plastic bottle recycling by developing a machine that turns them into filament for 3D printers
ENTRE_2023_POMOGI_TEXT: Initiative: students addressed the lack of funding for animal shelters by developing an app where users can choose a pet, care for it, and support it through donations
ENTRE_2023_FOOD_SAVING_TEXT: Initiative: students addressed food waste and financial losses for restaurants and stores by offering a platform with discounted products accessible to students
ENTRE_2023_AINA_TEXT: Initiative: students addressed the outflow of creative youth from Kazakhstan by proposing an initiative that strengthens interest in contemporary art and raises awareness of it within the country
WHY_BOX_FINAL: This is exactly what students learn at HTA
